title: Quick Revision: Is Matter Around Us Pure?

table: Made of only one kind of particle: an element or a compound
Uniform composition throughout, e.g. salt solution, air
Non-uniform composition, e.g. sand in water, oil and water
Homogeneous mixture of a solute in a solvent; particles too small to see; no Tyndall effect
Heterogeneous; particles visible and settle down, e.g. chalk in water
Particles too small to see but they scatter light (Tyndall effect) and do not settle, e.g. milk, fog

box: **Concentration (mass by mass %) = mass of solute ÷ mass of solution × 100**
Mass of solution = mass of solute + mass of solvent

table: Acetone and water (boiling points far apart)
Gases of the air; petroleum fractions (boiling points close)
Pure copper sulphate from impure sample

bullets: Iron filings mixed with sulphur powder: a **mixture**. A magnet pulls out the iron, and each keeps its own properties.
Heated together they form a **compound**, iron sulphide: Fe + S → FeS. It has new properties and a fixed composition, and a magnet cannot separate it.
